claims.text: W-based refractory high-entropy alloys can exhibit superconductivity at cryogenic temperatures.
Tungsten can enhance electron–phonon interactions within a homogeneous alloy matrix.
Controlled casting can produce a single-phase, homogeneous W-based refractory high-entropy alloy.
The alloy has an estimated superconducting critical temperature below approximately 2 K.
Minimizing external magnetic fields while cooling favors observation of the proposed superconducting state.
The alloy can retain a uniform microstructure during cryogenic cooling.
Tungsten atoms are uniformly distributed within an FCC or similar matrix in the proposed alloy.
Uniformly distributed tungsten enhances the electron–phonon coupling needed for superconductivity.
Tungsten's inherent characteristics can produce stronger electron–phonon coupling in a complex alloy.
Stronger electron–phonon coupling in the alloy can permit Cooper-pair formation below the critical temperature.
Cooper-pair formation can lead to the emergence of a superconducting phase in the alloy.
Cooling below the critical temperature will cause a transition to zero electrical resistance.
The proposed superconducting transition will be accompanied by magnetic-flux expulsion associated with the Meissner effect.
Well above the predicted critical temperature, the alloy exhibits normal metallic conduction and no superconducting behavior.
Phase separation or microstructural inhomogeneity can prevent the proposed superconductivity.
Impurities can disrupt the proposed tungsten-associated electron–phonon coupling.
A matrix that does not support coherent pairing over sufficient length scales will not sustain the proposed superconducting state.
Prior research specifically linking W-based high-entropy alloys to superconductivity is limited.
The exact critical temperature and robustness of the proposed superconducting phase are uncertain.
The absence of both zero resistance and Meissner flux exclusion below the expected critical temperature would falsify the superconductivity hypothesis.
